o1.biggest_strength: Puts the broken in-app checkout first with the money attached, and sizes every test honestly against the real traffic so I know these are big-lift-only tests.
o1.biggest_mistake: The lift figures on add-to-cart as the main metric leave me unsure whether a win on add-to-cart actually pays off in orders, since orders is only a loose guardrail.
o1.what_would_make_it_a_10: Tie each test's add-to-cart win to an expected order and rupee effect so I can rank by money, not just by evidence.

o2.biggest_strength: The funnel table by device and browser is the clearest read of where money leaks, and it makes orders-per-session the main metric, which is what actually pays.
o2.biggest_mistake: Running tests in parallel waves and changing two things in test 5 (first image and reviews) muddies what caused a win, and the 4-week runs on orders-per-session may still under-detect real effects.
o2.what_would_make_it_a_10: One change per test, a single sequential schedule, and a clear read on whether the estimated 10% detectable effect is realistic at this conversion rate.

reason: Both put the checkout bug and the money first, but Output 1 sequences the tests one at a time with cleaner maths and a stricter read on when to ship, so I trust its answers more when I'm about to spend weeks running them.
